about: Plot expressions in the forms the graph fence carries (the server's extractors write ** for ^ and keep glyphs such as −, √ and |) and a user types into the phone's series editor, with the y SymPy gives at each x through the server's own reading (app.modules.math.solve._parse_expression, the parse sample_function plots). apps/mobile/lib/math/graphExpr.ts re-reads the same text to resample on zoom and must agree within 1e-9 (relative above 1). A null y has no real, finite value there (outside the domain or at a pole): the phone must give NaN or an infinity, which its sampler drops. refused: neither side reads the text as a plot. phone_gap: the server reads it and the phone does not yet; the phone test skips its parity and checks the phone refuses rather than drawing a different curve. Delete the line when the phone learns it.

cases.note: Neither side reads a bracketless function before a power: SymPy's implicit application fails on it and the phone needs brackets. sin(x^2) and sin(x)^2 both read.

cases.phone_gap: The server reads a function name without brackets (SymPy implicit application: sin x is sin(x), cos 2x is cos(2x)). The phone parser needs the bracket, so it refuses and draws the server's own samples, which it cannot resample on zoom.

The server rewrites √ before parsing (_rewrite_unicode_sqrts). The phone tokenizer has no √, so it refuses and draws the server's own samples.
The server pairs bare bars into Abs (_rewrite_bare_abs_bars). The phone tokenizer has no |, so it refuses and draws the server's own samples.
The server splits the glued name xe into x times e (split_symbols). The phone reads xe as one unknown name, so it refuses and draws the server's own samples.
